Make we, we as a city, need to make an investment. And our investment is probably going to be on the legal enforcement side and getting in and starting with some of these landlords and getting those properties cleaned up. That's the investment. When you don't have investment, you have blight. And there are plenty of studies throughout there from urban studies, from Wharton that I've reviewed, that go on with the city of Philadelphia, studies that are now going on with Michigan State University dealing with the issues in Detroit and Flint. And every one of those studies will tell you, You don't make an investment, you're going to have blight. It's that simple. The relationship is inverse. It's an inverse relationship. So you make no investment, you have high levels of blight. You make a lot of investment, You're going to have low areas of blight. It's an inverse relationship. And so we need to get on page And we need to start thinking about making an investment In our city. I am highly recommending that these two attorneys come in and give a presentation to City Council. Contrary to what John Gaylis believes is that it wasn't clean, that just shows John Gaylis' refusal to accept what a very, very good lawyer has put in writing about his friend. The Dykema -Gossett report is beginning to reach attorneys that do do municipal law, and it is becoming one of the standards in the industry as to how to analyze a conflict of interest. Dykema -Gossett, when he did the report, he had no axe to grind, he had no hidden agenda, and he did his job as a professional. And in my opinion, his legal opinion stands with respect to determining liability in this particular matter. We decided to go forward with this matter to the Oakland County Sheriff's Office for further review Because once again, the city attorney interjected his opinion and felt that the Southline Police Department had a conflict of interest in processing the investigation. investigation. Somehow, the city attorney doesn't believe that Kivell has a conflict of interest when he voted on contracts that benefited his employer, but he believed that the South Lyon Police Department obviously would have a conflict if they had carried on with the investigation. Again, agendas at their best. So everyone knows that the Oakland County Sheriff's Department would not issue a warrant for Kivell's arrest because the county does not enforce civil documents. What What they do is they enforce criminal statutes. For example, the county would involve itself in enforcing, let's say, for example, domestic violence statutes. I don't know what people's experience on City Council is with domestic violence, but those are criminal statutes that clearly the Oakland County Prosecutor's Office would get involved in. They do not get involved in enforcing the City of South Lyons charter. charter. I would like to note that Kivell even apologized at one point and believed that the better practice would have been for him to disclose his conflict of interest, but quite frankly, my personal opinion is, and it's only my personal opinion, that Mr. Kivell knew what he was doing, he just did not expect to get caught. The Open Meetings Act clearly states in 15 .263, subsection 6, a person shall not, the word is mandatory, It says shall not be excluded from a meeting otherwise open to the public except for a breach of the peace actually committed at the meeting. And I don't believe that anybody who has a statutory right under the Open Meetings Act should feel under any obligation that they need to leave the room because somebody is speaking at a microphone in an open meeting. Additionally, I would like to remind the public that not too long ago we had a mayor's forum In which we had six or seven individuals sitting at a table. All of them had a microphone. They were being filmed. They answered questions and they did that in the public view. And as each person answered the question, they handed the microphone to the next person And nobody got up and left because other people weren't answering the questions. The way to have handled this, if certain individuals or whatever, I did not put this program together, But if you want to eliminate individuals from hearing answers That other individuals are going to make, The way that this could have been done was you could have staggered The individuals coming into the meeting. So, for example, the meeting could have started at 6 .30. At 6 .30, you could have had candidate number one come in and gone through his interview, And then you could have scheduled candidate number two to come in at 7 o 'clock, Candidate number three to come in at 7 .30. So there was a way to achieve that without a violation of the Open Meetings Act. I personally do not want to participate in any discussion excluding anyone from an open meetings. Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. Thank you, Maggie.

You never know why these situations come to you, but all I can say Is in terms of my encouragement to you, Joyce, is that sometimes we are put in a position in life Because that's where we're supposed to be at that time. So obviously you are supposed to be here with us at this time in your life. And I'm going to take advantage of everything that I can learn learn from you and from your lawyer. Additionally, I'd like to say tomorrow's Fat Tuesday, and it's Punschke Day, and there's no other place in town to go for Punschkes except for the South Lion Bakery. I am sure that they are there now getting ready. That's the only place that I've learned that you can get absolutely fresh Punschkes. There will be a line outside that door. My favorites, of course, are the Bavarian cream and blueberries, as if I didn't need anything more to eat. So for Fat Tuesday, please, please stop by the South Lane Bakery. They're just fabulous. Wednesday starts Ash Wednesday, and I always kind of like to stop at Lake Street Tavern on Ash Wednesday only because they have probably the best French onion soup that I think I have ever had. And so stop in, have some French onion soup on a cold winter day with a salad, And then head off to your services in the evening. Now, on Thursday, yes, once again, I'm eating at the Southline Hotel. I don't know if everybody knows this, but the Southline Hotel has a new menu only on the first Thursday of the month. It is their Polish dinner tour. It includes pierogies, it includes cabbage rolls and mashed potatoes and sauerkraut and kielbasa, and they had it last Thursday. They started serving at 6, and they were sold out under an hour. I could not believe that they sold out that fast. So obviously the South Lane Hotel has hit on a fabulous menu that is selling out well. On Friday, once again, I'm eating again, and yes, I am going to be going to St. Joe's for the fish fry. St. Joe's fish fry is probably one of the largest fish fries in the area. They will be serving between 500 and 600 individuals during the Lent season. And if you're going to go to the fish fry, you'll see a lot of people there. You do not have to be a member of the parish. You will see many, many, many, many people in the community in attendance at that fish fry. It starts at 4. The line starts at around 3 o 'clock or 3 .30. And when you're done, please stop down at the Lion Theater and top off your weekend with a fabulous, fabulous movie. So there really is no reason for you to go anywhere but downtown South Lion. There are plenty of places to eat. You could enjoy this season that we're having right now. And I say um you know put your boots on and uh travel uh downtown south lion and put a couple Pounds on and you can walk it off while you're walking around so um that's it for tonight and I'd like to say um uh what a great place that we live and good night to everyone thank you for Inviting all of us into your homes this evening I have a great start to the lenten season and we Will see you at the next meeting of the city of south lion so thank you and have a good week

So I want to thank all the parents and the grandparents that were out there two Fridays ago for everything that they did. I also had an opportunity to meet the new school resource officer for the South Lane High School, Officer Dorkin. What an incredible individual he is. And actually, myself and Rose Walton, Councilwoman Rose Walton, we had to wait in line to meet him Because he was swarmed by the students that were introducing him to their friends and to their parents. It was incredible. This guy already has a fan club. So I was very, very impressed with him. He was just very, very committed to the students in South Lyon. In fact, I was surprised to learn that the Oakland County Sheriff was all over the football field As they are now the law enforcement agency at all the football games. And everybody I spoke to was absolutely excited to see the Oakland County Sheriff over there at the football games. So thank you Sheriff Bouchard Thank you for the gentleman that you sent in for this football team for the football game including Officer Dorkins as the pumpkin fest. I want to remind everyone that the craft show is at Bartlett Elementary I also want to thank all the volunteers who are going to be working at the chicken barbecue barbecue from 1130 till two o 'clock in the afternoon at the United Methodist Church. This will be a sellout. It always is. And they do a takeout. This is a fabulous barbecue dinner. I usually get four takeouts, two for Saturday and two for Sunday. I will tell you this will be a sellout event. So if you want to get a chicken dinner, get over there early. I'd also like to thank Pete's True Value for installing an American flag out in front of their business. Also Peter's True value also offers a military discount to veterans so please everybody shop local and Remember the good patriots at peter's true value hardware store located within the city limits of South lion and last we are all waiting with anticipation for our new city manager paul Zelnak to come and take a seat here and in council chambers we only have maybe about a week to go I I know the surrounding communities can hardly wait for him to arrive. I know the employees are anxious, and I know I am, So I think it's going to be very, very exciting for everybody to have a new face in town. Everybody has a lot of confidence in him, and everybody is waiting for him to come into the city. So we only have another week to go, so we're almost out of the fog. Other than that, I'd like to thank everyone for inviting us into your home this evening. Have a great week. Please go to Pumpkin Fest. I want to meet everybody. I think you're gonna have a great time It's gonna be just a super weekend to be in Southland and not go home until Monday morning. So, thank you

And the only way they can get those numbers and get their debt ratio down is to get a tax abatement. So I will scrutinize documentation when it comes in because that tends to indicate weakness in ability to finance the project Because you're looking for a lot of opportunities to reduce your debt load and sort of find somebody else to help pay your loan. That's basically what's going on in the big picture. That's the first issue. The second issue that I would scrutinize with this company would be cash flow is Many times when you are rehabbing you may be rehabbing for a specific purpose And you may have a business that's coming in that you don't have a track Record with so what you are attempting to do with the tax abatement is to Ensure that you have a sufficient cash flow to meet your tax liabilities so if So if your tax liabilities are high, then you have more risk in the tenant that comes into your space. But if you can get a tax abatement, then you are lowering your risk, and banks like lowered risk. So that, again, speaks to the strength of the borrower's ability to manage and handle a cash flow. So those are kind of the two issues that I would look at, is that if it appears that the financial strength is not there, then maybe the person has overpromised.
